name: CardFaro – Digital Business Cards · NFC & QR
author: bonanno

sections.description:
Your business card. Your website. Your data.

CardFaro creates digital business cards directly on your own WordPress website. Your contact data is stored and managed in your WordPress installation instead of on a central CardFaro card-hosting platform. You stay in control of your hosting, content and publication settings without needing an additional cloud platform or a mandatory subscription.

Design your digital business card with contact details, an introduction, portrait, logo and custom colors. Share it through NFC, a QR code or a link. Visitors can open the card in their browser and download a vCard to add your details to their address book.

Update your information at any time in the CardFaro editor. The published page URL stays the same, helping existing NFC tags and printed QR codes keep working.

Features

  • Self-hosted card data in your own WordPress database, with no central CardFaro cloud required to publish the card.
  • No transfer of stored card records to CardFaro servers, no built-in visitor tracking and no remotely loaded fonts.
  • QR codes generated locally in the browser without an external QR-code service.
  • A standalone editor for your digital business card, with no external CardFaro account registration or trial expiry. CardFaro Free requires no subscription.
  • Contact details, organization, introduction, portrait and logo from your Media Library, with clear remove and optional permanent-delete actions.
  • Custom colors, brand text and two-line slogan.
  • German and English contact pages with browser language selection and manual switching.
  • Public, non-indexed or protected visibility with a separate NFC/QR key and manual access code.
  • vCard 3.0 download, QR code display and SVG download, and native sharing or clipboard support.
  • Optional links to your privacy policy and legal notice.
  • No public card listing and no automatic menu links.
  • Control over the hosting, content and publication of your card through your WordPress installation.

Editor language

The CardFaro editor is available in German and English. Its language follows a saved manual CardFaro choice, then a supported WordPress user language, then the site language, and otherwise English. The editor, live preview and public contact page can use different languages without changing one another.

NFC and printed cards

CardFaro does not write NFC tags or provide physical cards. Write the contact page URL to a compatible tag with a suitable app or device, or print its QR code on your physical card. Hardware and NFC writing software are not included.

Privacy

CardFaro follows a self-hosted, data-conscious approach. The card record is stored in your own WordPress database, and CardFaro does not require a central CardFaro cloud or external card-hosting platform to publish it. Stored card records are not sent to CardFaro servers. CardFaro includes no visitor tracking or analytics, loads no external fonts and generates QR codes locally without contacting an external QR-code provider.

This differs from card services that store and serve contact profiles through their own hosted platform. With CardFaro, you control the WordPress installation, hosting provider, content and publication settings. CardFaro Free has no recurring user fee or mandatory subscription. Your WordPress hosting and any separately purchased services remain subject to their own terms and costs.

Only information you choose to publish appears on the contact page. Public cards may be indexed. “Do not index” asks search engines not to index the page but is not access protection. Protected cards require their NFC/QR key or manual code and remember access in that browser for 30 days. Unpublish the card to stop CardFaro from serving its contact details.

Portraits and logos are selected from the WordPress Media Library. WordPress media files remain directly accessible through their file URL even when used on a protected card. Remove a file from the Media Library if it must no longer be publicly accessible. CardFaro removes a local file only after explicit confirmation and only when no other CardFaro card or global setting still uses it. CardFaro cannot detect every use by posts, themes or other plugins.

Deactivating or deleting the plugin preserves the saved contact record. To remove it permanently, unpublish the card, clear its fields and save before removing the plugin. Remove uploaded media separately when appropriate.

The privacy and data-sovereignty properties of the complete website also depend on your hosting provider, WordPress configuration, theme and other plugins. CardFaro does not claim that installing the plugin alone makes a website compliant with any particular privacy law.

Documentation and support: https://cardfaro.de/support/

Third-party code

QR code generation uses the MIT-licensed QR Code generator library by Project Nayuki, bundled locally. Source and license: https://www.nayuki.io/page/qr-code-generator-library
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate CardFaro.
  2. Open CardFaro in your WordPress administration menu.
  3. Enter your contact details and choose a URL name using lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens.
  4. Select “Make this contact page public” and save.
  5. Open the contact page to download its QR code as an SVG for printing and download the vCard.

If a contact URL returns a 404 after activation, visit Settings > Permalinks and save once. No changes to the permalink structure are required.
sections.faq:
Does the free version stop working after a trial?

No. This standalone single-contact plugin has no trial expiry or paid feature gates.

Do I need an external account?

No. The free contact page is managed and hosted by your WordPress installation.

Where is my business card data stored?

The card record is stored in your own WordPress installation. A central CardFaro cloud is not required to store or publish the card. Your hosting provider and other components of your WordPress website may process data under their own terms.

Is CardFaro a privacy-friendly alternative to cloud-hosted business card services?

CardFaro takes a data-conscious, self-hosted approach: card records stay in your WordPress database, QR codes are generated locally, and CardFaro includes no visitor tracking, analytics or remotely loaded fonts. This gives you more direct control than a centrally hosted card platform. The privacy compliance of your website still depends on your hosting, configuration, theme, other plugins and how you use and publish personal data.

Can I change details after printing a QR code?

Yes. Edit your contact details and keep the existing page URL. Changing your domain or moving your WordPress site may require redirects or rewriting your tags.

Does this plugin write an NFC tag?

No. Use an NFC writing app or compatible writer to store the contact-page URL on your tag.

Is the editor available in English?

Yes. The editor, live preview and public contact page support German and English. The editor language is stored per WordPress user only after a manual choice and does not change the WordPress user language.

Does unpublishing delete my contact?

No. The saved contact remains in the editor, but the public contact endpoint stops serving it.
sections.changelog:
1.2.4

  • Added clear portrait and logo actions for choosing, uploading and removing Media Library images.
  • Preserved external image URLs as a fallback and kept existing cards and URL-only records unchanged.
  • Added optional permanent Media Library deletion with a second confirmation and CardFaro reference checks.
  • Added a discreet CardFaro Pro information section at the end of the Free editor only.

1.2.3

  • Preserved the selected language when submitting a protected-card access code.
  • Changed NFC/QR unlocking to submit the key by POST instead of placing it in the query string.
  • Reloads the access page after the 15-second cooldown so the warning disappears automatically.
  • Protected cards display portrait and logo after authorization and clarify that existing WordPress Media Library files remain directly public and should be removed when that is not intended.

1.2.2

  • Fixed NFC/QR fragment unlocking and manual access-code verification.
  • Added a card-specific 15-second cooldown after an incorrect manual code.
  • Fixed the portrait position on cards without a cover slogan.

1.2.1

  • Restored the historical noindex behavior as the default for new and legacy cards without an explicit visibility setting.

1.2.0

  • Added public, non-indexed and protected card visibility in Free and Pro.
  • Added cryptographically random NFC/QR keys, separate manual codes and card-specific 30-day browser grants.
  • Added rate limiting, key rotation, vCard protection and strict no-cache/security headers.

1.1.1

  • Updated the WordPress administration menu to use the current CardFaro logo.

1.1.0

  • Added a complete German and English editor with per-user language selection.
  • Added a shared live preview with an independent German/English switch.
  • Added up to 20 bilingual additional links with optional English destination URLs.
  • Made public pages, vCards, website and legal links use consistent language and URL rules.
  • Preserved stable public card URLs and vCard UIDs during the upgrade.

1.0.1

  • Updated product and support information and expanded NFC setup guidance.
  • Clarified how public card URLs, search indexing and contact data work.

1.0.0

  • Initial standalone single-contact release.
